_comment: Wave 137 — a 10e battle lasts five battle rounds; a one-sided tabling does NOT end it early. Source: Wahapedia 10e core rules, 'The Battle Round'.

simulator.battle_length_five_rounds.rule_name: The battle lasts five battle rounds
simulator.battle_length_five_rounds.quoted_text: Games of Warhammer 40,000 are played over five battle rounds. In each battle round, both players take a turn.
simulator.battle_length_five_rounds.trigger: end of each scored battle round in Battle.run(): decide whether to continue to the next round
simulator.battle_length_five_rounds.effect: the battle plays out the full five battle rounds and only ends early on a MUTUAL wipe (both armies have nothing left on-board and nothing in reserves). A one-sided tabling does NOT end the game — the surviving army keeps playing the remaining rounds and scoring primary on the uncontested board (bounded by the 50-VP primary cap). Previously the loop broke on EITHER side reaching zero, truncating the tabler's continued scoring (a VP / Stage-2-pricing fidelity gap that could also flip an edge case where the tabler trailed on VP at the tabling moment).
